sources.version: Vertebrate Zoology 71:27-48; version of record published 2021-02-26
sources.locator: Abstract; Morphological comparisons, pp. 34-35; Integrative species delimitation, pp. 35-37; lectotype designation and discussion of P. bastardi, pp. 38-43
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated on article page 27

Completing a taxonomic puzzle: integrative review of geckos of the Paroedura bastardi species complex (Squamata, Gekkonidae). Vertebrate Zoology 71:27-48. https://doi.org/10.3897/vz.71.e59495. Claims are paraphrased; article CC BY 4.0.

claims.text: In the sampled adult and subadult comparisons, measured body-size values overlapped among lineages and the authors found that no single reported ratio was unambiguously diagnostic for each species. They caution that the ratios have limited value for reliable field identification.
claims.placeTimeScope: Morphological comparison in the 2021 study, using its sampled adult and subadult specimens; it is not a complete species-wide diagnosis.
claims.lifeStatus: Adult and subadult specimens; juvenile morphology and unmeasured variation are not inferred.

gaps: The study reports overlapping measurements and limited sampling; it does not provide a complete account of morphology or variation across the accepted species concept.
No life-cycle, reproductive, growth, survival or longevity evidence was assessed.
The source is an integrative taxonomic revision and does not provide a bounded ecological assessment for the currently restricted accepted species concept.

claims.text: The authors recovered multiple distinct P. bastardi lineages from their mitochondrial and nuclear analyses and report syntopic occurrences without genetic admixture or morphological intermediates as evidence supporting reproductive isolation among sampled lineages. The lineage-level result does not imply that all historically assigned P. bastardi populations belong to the currently accepted species concept.
claims.placeTimeScope: Multilocus analyses and sampled sympatric localities in Madagascar reported in 2021; interpretation is limited to sampled lineages and markers.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild collected specimens; no broader population-wide inference is made.

gaps: The authors note that denser phylogenomic study is needed; evolutionary history outside the sampled complex and accepted concept remains unassessed.

claims.text: After designating a lectotype, the authors restrict P. bastardi sensu stricto to the extreme south-east of Madagascar. This is the range conclusion of the 2021 revision and is not presented as a current exhaustive range inventory.
claims.locator: Abstract; lectotype designation and discussion of P. bastardi, pp. 38-43
claims.placeTimeScope: Madagascar records examined for the 2021 taxonomic revision; no post-publication range survey is represented.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild locality records reviewed by the authors.

gaps: No current, exhaustive occurrence-data or range-boundary assessment was conducted.
No fossil evidence or bounded fossil-literature search was assessed.
No dated conservation assessment or population-trend analysis was reviewed; no risk category is inferred.

reasons: The selected revision provides bounded taxonomic, morphological, lineage and distribution evidence; life history, ecology, fossils and conservation remain unassessed.
The source's historical P. bastardi usage contains multiple lineages, so its claims require careful restriction to the lectotype-defined concept.
No systematic current literature search or independent expert review has been completed.

claims.text: The authors report that P. tanjaka and P. neglecta share the diagnostic state of having the nostril contact the rostral scale, separating the pair from other members of the species group considered. This character does not distinguish P. tanjaka from P. neglecta.
claims.locator: Morphological comparisons, p. 34; diagnosis reference to Köhler et al. (2019)
claims.placeTimeScope: Diagnostic character as reported in the 2021 revision; this is a limited character statement rather than a complete diagnosis.
claims.lifeStatus: Morphological character; the claim does not assert variation across all ages or populations.

gaps: The article identifies one diagnostic character and does not establish the full range of morphological variation for P. tanjaka.
No life-cycle, reproductive, growth, survival or longevity evidence was assessed.

claims.text: The revision reports P. tanjaka and P. neglecta as sympatric at Bemaraha; the two were recovered as distinct mitochondrial lineages and shared no nuclear haplotypes in the study's markers. This documents co-occurrence in the sampled locality, not a complete ecological relationship or range-wide pattern.
claims.locator: Integrative species delimitation, sympatry in Bemaraha, pp. 35-36
claims.placeTimeScope: Specimens and locality records from Bemaraha analyzed in the 2021 study.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild collected specimens; no captive behavior is inferred.

gaps: The study does not provide a systematic ecological account or establish the full habitat range and interactions of P. tanjaka.

claims.text: In the study's mitochondrial and nuclear analyses, P. tanjaka formed a distinct lineage from sympatric P. neglecta, and the authors placed the two as sister species in their phylogenetic hypothesis. They note that relationships in this group need confirmation through more comprehensive phylogenomic study.
claims.locator: Abstract; multilocus phylogenetic relationships, pp. 33-34; sympatry in Bemaraha, pp. 35-36
claims.placeTimeScope: Phylogenetic hypothesis based on the paper's sampled loci and specimens; the authors identify the need for further phylogenomic study.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild sampled specimens; no broader evolutionary rate or population inference is made.

gaps: No later phylogenomic confirmation or comparative evolutionary synthesis was assessed.

claims.text: The authors describe P. tanjaka as known only from the karstic Tsingy de Bemaraha in central-west Madagascar in the study's taxonomic background.
claims.locator: Introduction, p. 28; sympatry in Bemaraha, pp. 35-36
claims.placeTimeScope: Distribution statement in the 2021 paper; it is not a current exhaustive occurrence inventory.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild locality records considered in the revision.

gaps: No current exhaustive range survey, boundary assessment or native-versus-introduced analysis was conducted.
No fossil evidence or bounded fossil-literature search was assessed.
No dated conservation assessment or population-trend analysis was reviewed; no risk category is inferred.

reasons: The single selected taxonomic revision provides limited morphology, locality, sympatry and phylogenetic evidence; life history, fossils and conservation remain unassessed, and ecology is partial.
No systematic current literature search or independent expert review has been completed.
